reading.review:
A masterclass in collective biography. Doris Kearns Goodwin traces how Abraham Lincoln invited his sharpest 1860 rivals — Seward, Chase, and Bates — into his Cabinet and won their trust through patience, humor, and generosity of credit.

Despite its length, the narrative reads like a brisk drama and offers timeless lessons on listening to dissenting voices.
